notes: Table 2 maps each LMST_HVS name to its J designation (T:p5-b1), and Table 1 gives the same J designations. LMST HVS3 is additionally catalogued as NLTT 309-34 (T:p6-b2). HIP 60350 (LAMOST J122229.60+404935.5) is not one of the final 28, but it is a previously known 'hyper-runaway B-type star' that the paper rechecks and compares with Irrgang et al.; it is therefore included as follow_up, with no current boundness reassessment (T:p3-b7, T:p4-b0, I:p3-b0). The 28 new objects are candidates_found because the paper explicitly calls them HVS candidates, reports Vgt > 300 km/s for the sample, and retains them in its final assessment (T:p1-b3, T:p2-b1, T:p2-b11, T:p4-b16).

LMST_HVS1: Target star identified as LMST_HVS1 (J085819.90+150352.4). Table 3 prints D⊙ in kpc, but the tabulated values (e.g., 1462 for LMST_HVS1) are incompatible with the kpc scale and with the paper's solar-neighborhood context; I record the Table 3 distance as 1462 pc and flag this apparent unit error. No bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

LMST_HVS2: Table 3 (T:p6-b0) lists no literature-based distance or velocity for LMST_HVS2 (all entries are dashes), so no values from that table were extracted. The two radial velocities come from different reductions (LAMOST 1D pipeline versus IRAF) and are both retained. No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS3: LMST_HVS3 is identified with J074233.15+322433.8 and NLTT 309-34 (T:p6-b2). The paper reports two independent proper-motion sets and two radial-velocity reductions; these are retained separately. In the literature-comparison table, the LMST_HVS3 row lists dashes for distance and all kinematic quantities, so no additional Table 3 values are included (T:p6-b0).

LMST_HVS4: Target identified as LMST_HVS4 = J225922.58+262409.9 (row 4 of Tables 1-3). Table 3 (T:p6-b0) prints its heliocentric-distance column header as 'D☉ kpc', but the entries (e.g., 1329 for this star, 1462 for LMST_HVS1) are only consistent with parsecs, both from the magnitude of the values and from the paper's repeated statement that all candidates lie at heliocentric distances of less than ~3 kpc (Table 2 gives 0.9 kpc for the same star). I therefore record the literature distance as 1329 pc and flag this unit inconsistency. Radial velocities are given for two reductions in Table 1 (LAMOST 1D pipeline and authors' IRAF reduction); neither is preferred here. No parallax, bound/unbound probability, or Galactic-rest-frame velocity based on the Local Standard of Rest is reported for this star. Table 1 does not list RV uncertainties for this object.

LMST_HVS5: Table 3 (T:p6-b0) is headed D⊙ in kpc but lists 1010 for LMST_HVS5, while Table 2 (T:p5-b1) gives 1.1 kpc for the same star; I retain the Table 3 value and its stated unit exactly as printed, without conversion. No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS6: For LMST_HVS6 / J082932.48+282613.3, Table 3 lists dashes for its literature distance and velocity components, so no additional literature distance or velocity values are extracted. Two proper-motion determinations are reported: UCAC4 in Table 1 and NLTT in Section 4. Two radial velocities are reported: LAMOST-pipeline and IRAF-reduction values.

LMST_HVS7: Target identified as LMST_HVS7 = J231232.05+265039.5. In T:p5-b0 (Table 1), two radial-velocity determinations are listed for this row, V_r^a from the LAMOST 1D pipeline and V_r^b from the IRAF reduction; both are retained, and no per-star RV uncertainty is given there. In T:p5-b1 (Table 2), the distance D⊙ = 1.6 kpc is the paper's photometric distance; the text states a typical photometric distance accuracy of about 10%, but no individual error is reported for this star. Table 3 (T:p6-b0) shows dashes for LMST_HVS7's literature distance and velocities, so no additional literature-based values are retained. No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this target.

LMST_HVS8: Table 3 (T:p6-b0) labels the distance column D_sun as "kpc", but the entries for this and other stars (e.g., 130 to 5099) and the paper's sample of stars within about 3 kpc make the column internally inconsistent; the values are evidently in pc. I therefore record the Table 3 literature distances as pc while noting the reported header. Parenthetical entries in Table 3 are values from Ref. 2, while entries before the parentheses are from Ref. 1. No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS9: Table 3 labels its D⊙ column as kpc, but the tabulated values (2475 for LMST_HVS9 and 130–5099 for the sample) and the paper's nearby-HVS context indicate the values are in pc; the literature distance is therefore recorded as 2475 pc (T:p6-b0, T:p6-b4). No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star. The two Table 1 radial velocities are retained separately because they come from different reductions (T:p5-b0).

LMST_HVS10: Target star: LMST_HVS10 = J110208.65+575200.2. The paper reports two radial velocities for this star (LAMOST 1D pipeline -219 km/s and IRAF-based -227 km/s, Table 1); both are retained. Two distances/space velocities are reported: the authors' own photometric distance (0.8 kpc, Table 2) with V_gt = 423 ± 35 km/s, and a literature-distance-based recalculation (Table 3, ref. 1 = Pickles & Depagne 2010) giving V_gt = 250 km/s; both are retained. The Table 3 entry lists D_sun = "130" in a column headed "kpc"; this is inconsistent with the paper's own 0.8 kpc distance for this star and with the kpc-scale values (1000-5000) of the other Table 3 entries, so the value appears to be printed in pc despite the column heading. Because the reported unit and the numerical value are contradictory, this distance is omitted from the distance quantity (T:p6-b0, I:p6-b0); the associated literature-based V_gt (=250 km/s) is retained since it is unaffected by the unit ambiguity. No parallax, bound/unbound probability, or other velocity components are given per star beyond those listed.
LMST_HVS11: Table 3 lists no additional literature distance or velocity values for LMST_HVS11 (entries are dashes).

LMST_HVS12: Table 1 reports two radial velocities for LMST_HVS12: V_r^a = -219 km s^-1 from the LAMOST 1D pipeline and V_r^b = -195 km s^-1 from the authors' IRAF reduction (T:p5-b0); both are retained. Table 3's D⊙ column is printed with unit kpc, but the entries are evidently parsecs (LMST_HVS12 has D⊙ = 1.4 kpc in Table 2 and 2468 in Table 3; LMST_HVS1 similarly has 3.3 kpc in Table 2 and 1462 in Table 3). The Table 3 literature distance is therefore recorded as 2468 pc with this unit inconsistency flagged (T:p6-b0). Table 1's RA proper-motion component is explicitly μa cos(δ), retained as reported (T:p5-b0).

LMST_HVS13: For LMST_HVS13, Table 2 (T:p5-b1) gives D⊙ = 1.3 kpc and V_gt = 354 ± 18 km/s, while Table 3 (T:p6-b0) gives a literature-based distance of 2378 with Ref. 1 (Pickles & Depagne 2010) and V_gt = 534 km/s. Table 3's supplied header labels the distance column as kpc, but 2378 kpc is inconsistent with the star's apparent magnitude, proper motion, Table 2 distance, and the tabulated space velocity; I therefore interpret that column's values as pc and preserve the printed number 2378. No parallax or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

LMST_HVS14: Table 3 (T:p6-b0, I:p6-b0) is titled as giving distances "D_sun kpc", but its entries (e.g., 1484 and 1267 for LMST_HVS14, 1462 for LMST_HVS1) are evidently in pc: the paper states these are literature photometric distances for nearby HVS candidates, and interpreting them as kpc would give galactocentric distances far beyond the Galaxy. I therefore record 1484 and 1267 with unit pc; the printed column header unit (kpc) is not used. No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS15: Table 3's D⊙ column is transcribed with unit “kpc” in T:p6-b0/I:p6-b0, but the LMST_HVS15 entry is 798; this is consistent with 798 pc, with Table 2's 0.8 kpc, and with the paper's statement that candidates are at heliocentric distances <3 kpc. I therefore record the Table 3 distance in pc and flag the reported unit inconsistency. Table 1 gives two radial velocities (LAMOST 1D pipeline and IRAF reduction) without per-star uncertainties; both are retained.

LMST_HVS16: Table 3 lists LMST_HVS16 but gives no literature distance or velocity values for it (all em dashes), so none were extracted from that table (T:p6-b0). The two radial velocities correspond to two reductions (LAMOST pipeline and IRAF), not alternative best values. No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS17: T:p5-b0: Table 1 reports two radial velocities, V_r^a (LAMOST 1D pipeline) and V_r^b (IRAF); both are retained. The same R.A./Dec. values are repeated in Tables 1–3 and are retained once. T:p6-b0: Table 3 lists D⊙ under a “kpc” header, but the target value 1031 and the paper's nearby-star distances indicate parsecs; that literature distance is recorded as 1031 pc without converting the number.

LMST_HVS18: For LMST_HVS18 / J173650.63+060814.4, Table 3 lists dashes for D⊙ and all derived velocities, so no literature-based values are retained. Table 1 gives two radial-velocity determinations (LAMOST 1D pipeline and IRAF) without individual uncertainties, and both are recorded. The Table 2 distance is reported as 0.4 kpc with one decimal place.

LMST_HVS19: T:p5-b0 gives two radial velocities for LMST_HVS19: V_r^a (LAMOST 1D pipeline) = -462 km/s and V_r^b (IRAF reduction) = -436 km/s; both are retained. T:p6-b0 labels the Table 3 D⊙ column in kpc, but the LMST_HVS19 entry (3658) is far outside the nearby-star context and would be physically inconsistent with the tabulated velocity unless the intended unit were pc; the printed value and unit are retained and flagged as a likely unit misprint.

LMST_HVS20: Table 3's D_⊙ column is headed "kpc" at T:p6-b0, but its listed distances (e.g., 1455 and 596 for LMST_HVS20) are incompatible with the paper's <3 kpc sample and evidently are in pc; I retain the printed numbers and record the unit as pc. In Table 3, the values outside and inside parentheses correspond to references 1 and 2, respectively, as indicated by the Ref. entry "1(2)" at T:p6-b0.

LMST_HVS21: Target identified as LMST_HVS21 = J122723.65+482136.1 (Table 1 designation J122723.65+482136.1; Tables 2 and 3 list the same object as LMST_HVS21). Two radial velocities are reported: LAMOST 1D pipeline (-209 km/s) and the authors' IRAF reduction (-213 km/s); the paper's adopted RV for the kinematic analysis is the IRAF-based value (V_r^b), and no individual uncertainty is given in Table 1 for this star. The Figure 1 spectrum labelled J122723.65+482136.1 shows rv = -213 km/s, consistent with V_r^b. Table 3 (T:p6-b0, I:p6-b0) has a column header "D_sun kpc" but the entries (130, 798, 1010 ... 5099) and their comparison with the kpc-scale distances in Table 2 (0.2-3.3 kpc) indicate the column values are in pc; therefore the literature-based distance for this star is recorded as 5099 pc with the printed unit noted. The Table 3 velocity recomputed from that distance (2015 km/s) is much larger than the Table 2 value (323 km/s); both are reported as distinct results without choosing a preferred one. No parallax, distance modulus, bound/unbound probability, or total rest-frame velocity other than V_gt is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS22: Table 3's D⊙ column is labeled kpc in T:p6-b0/I:p6-b0, but its values (e.g., 130, 1462, 2422) are evidently parsecs and are consistent with the paper's kpc-scale distances; the HVS22 literature distance is therefore recorded as 2422 pc with this apparent unit misprint noted. Both reported radial velocities are included because Table 1 gives two reductions. No annual parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS23: Table 1 lists two radial velocities for LMST_HVS23: V_r^a = -203 km/s from the LAMOST 1D pipeline and V_r^b = -197 km/s from the authors' IRAF reduction; both are retained under their respective conditions. Table 3's D⊙ column is labeled "kpc" in T:p6-b0, but its entries (1204 for LMST_HVS23 and values up to 5099) are evidently parsecs; the paper's Table 2 gives 1.2 kpc for the same star in T:p5-b1. I therefore record the Table 3 literature distance as 1204 pc without changing the reported number.

LMST_HVS24: Target: LMST_HVS24 / J212028.30-013323.4. Table 1 (T:p5-b0) reports two radial velocities, from the LAMOST 1D pipeline and the IRAF reduction; both are retained. Table 3 (T:p6-b0) contains dashes rather than literature-based distance or velocity values for this target, so no additional values from that table are included. No parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LMST_HVS25: T:p6-b0: the Table 3 D_sun column is headed "kpc", but its listed values (e.g., 2415 for LMST_HVS25) are evidently in pc, since Table 2 gives 1.9 kpc for the same star; I retain the reported number 2415 and label its unit as pc. T:p5-b0: two radial velocities are reported for this target, from the LAMOST 1D pipeline and the IRAF reduction.

LMST_HVS26: For LMST_HVS26 (J065436.50+170313.8), Table 1 reports two distinct radial velocities, both retained above: V_r^a = 290 km/s from the LAMOST 1D pipeline and V_r^b = 307 km/s from the authors' IRAF reduction. Table 3 lists this star but gives dashes for its literature distance and velocity columns, so no Table 3 values were extracted. No annual parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this target.

LMST_HVS27: The D⊙ column in Table 3 is headed “kpc” (T:p6-b0; image I:p6-b0), but its values, such as 1878 for LMST_HVS27, are evidently in pc: they are literature photometric distances and are inconsistent with the paper’s <3 kpc sample and with the 0.7 kpc value in Table 2. I retain the reported number 1878 and record its unit as pc. No parallax or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

LMST_HVS28: T:p6-b0: Table 3's D⊙ column is headed “kpc,” but its values (e.g., 1698 for LMST_HVS28) are evidently in pc; I retain the printed unit and flag the inconsistency. Table 1 gives no individual radial-velocity uncertainties for this star.

HIP 60350: The target HIP 60350 is matched to LAMOST designation J122229.60+404935.5 in T:p3-b7. Only radial velocities are reported for this star in the supplied material; it is not among the entries in Tables 1–3. The top panel of Figure 1 (I:p3-b0) labels J122229.60+404935.5 with rv=257 km s−1, consistent with the IRAF value in the text; the distinct literature value is retained separately.
